text:
I gave Elon Musk's new Grok Bot my content calendar instead of a to-do list, and in one week I stopped being a creator who does the work and became one who reviews it.

seven bots. one shared machine. nobody edits but me. here's the whole design, save it.

step 1 → 0:00 what one shared computer changes
step 2 → 0:11 spinning up the first bot
step 3 → 2:38 wiring plugins and delegation
step 4 → 4:02 slack + routines
step 5 → 6:15 freezing the workflow into a skill

THE ROSTER:

Anchor, chief of staff. the only bot I dm. I hand it rough ideas, it decomposes them into research, draft, visuals, publish, and posts the shipping list to the group chat every morning. never writes itself.

Radar, discovery. every morning: 20 topics moving in my niche, one line on why each is hot, and a source. flags anything already covered to death. if it can't verify the trend, it says so.

Digger, research. takes a topic and returns a fact sheet. claims with sources, contrarian angles, three quotes I can actually use. one warning at the top for anything it couldn't confirm.

Ink, writing. turns Digger's sheet into a draft in my voice. keeps a swipe file of my last 40 posts and matches rhythm. 900 words max for a post, 60 for a caption. queued in drafts, I approve in bulk.

Studio, visuals. builds thumbnails, headers, and inline graphics. always three options, always named for the angle they push, never the fourth safe one.

Loop, distribution. once I approve, ships to Substack, cross-posts to X and LinkedIn, schedules the follow-up thread for 24h later. never invents a claim I didn't write.

Mirror, analyst. one report a night. what got opened, what got shared, what died, and the single number I should care about tomorrow. no dashboards, no adjectives.

HOW THEY'RE WIRED
one group chat per post, not per bot. Anchor sits in all of them. the bots hand off inside the chat, so I only read the final draft. I never route the work.

two rules that made this actually work:
1. every routine ends with a hard "do not publish without approval" line. autonomy without a fence is chaos on a schedule.
2. show once, don't describe. I ran the full workflow on my screen one time and let them watch. that single demo taught them more than a page of instructions ever could.

WEEK ONE
25 drafts written. 14 shipped. 6 killed on read-through. 44 thumbnails proposed, 15 picked. inbox at zero every morning. one report I forwarded to a client without editing a word.

THE POINT
most people are still treating Grok Bot like a smarter chat window. it isn't. it's the first time one person can own an org chart instead of a to-do list. my bottleneck was never how much I could do, it was how much I could hand off.

bookmark this.
